title: Language Models as Few-Shot Learners
relevance: Original paper establishing in-context learning as a paradigm; foundational for understanding ICL capabilities and limitations through GPT-3's few-shot results.

title: Transformers as Algorithms: A Theoretical Framework for In-Context Learning
relevance: Formal theoretical analysis showing transformers can implement gradient descent and other learning algorithms in-context; key for understanding theoretical limits of ICL.

title: What Can Transformers Learn In-Context? A Case Study of Simple Functions
relevance: Empirical demonstration that transformers can learn linear functions and polynomial regression in-context; reveals both capabilities and failure modes of ICL.

title: In-Context Learning Creates Flat Minima
relevance: Connects ICL to meta-learning theory; argues transformers implicitly optimize for flat loss basins during pretraining, enabling few-shot generalization.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
relevance: Analyzes how chain-of-thought prompting extends ICL to multi-step reasoning; documents where it helps versus where it fails; essential for understanding ICL boundaries.

title: Larger Language Models Don't Always Beat Smaller Ones: An Investigation into the Inherent Capabilities of Smaller Language Models
relevance: Careful empirical work showing ICL is not monotonically improving with scale; certain tasks favor smaller models; complicates naive scaling assumptions.

title: Dealing with Parenthesis in Large Language Models: The Case of In-Context Learning
relevance: Studies length generalization failures in transformers; provides a clear example of when ICL breaks down and why; key evidence for ICL's interpolation limits.

title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
relevance: Argues models converge on shared representations; relevant to understanding whether ICL reflects genuine abstraction or surface pattern matching.

title: In-Context Learning May Not Always Be What You Need
relevance: Shows fine-tuning often outperforms ICL for specific task distributions; provides crucial contrast for understanding when each paradigm is appropriate.

title: In-Context Learning Does Not What You Think It Does: Retrieving Learned Patterns from In-Context
relevance: Ablation study showing many apparent ICL capabilities may be retrieval from training data rather than genuine generalization; critical for interpreting ICL results.

title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
relevance: Documents capabilities emerging at scale; discusses which abilities are continuous versus discontinuous; essential for understanding ICL scaling behavior.

title: Scaling Laws for In-Context Learning
relevance: Derives scaling laws specifically for few-shot performance; predicts compute-optimal context size; provides quantitative limits on ICL capability.

title: Formal Limitations of Transformers in Learning Context-Dependent Rules
relevance: Early theoretical work on what formal languages transformers can and cannot learn in-context; computational complexity perspective on ICL limits.

title: What Features Are Learned in In-Context Learning? A Comprehensive Analysis
relevance: Probing analysis to determine what representations enable ICL; distinguishes semantic memory from working-memory-like processing; mechanistic understanding of ICL.

title: An Analysis of the In-Context Learning Task in Transformers
relevance: Investigates mechanistic details of how attention patterns encode task structure during ICL; provides detailed understanding of the computation.

title: In-Context Learning with Neural Tangent Kernel Theory
relevance: Connects ICL to NTK theory; provides theoretical framework for understanding when and why transformers generalize in-context.
